questions.explain: Moving pollen by hand allows fertilisation.

questions.prompt: You want new plants EXACTLY like your best mango tree. Which method?
questions.explain: Seeds mix features from two parents; vegetative methods copy one.

questions.prompt: Which actions help pollinators such as bees and butterflies? Choose all that apply.
options: Planting a variety of nectar-rich flowers
questions.explain: Pollinators need food, water and safety.

questions.prompt: Many crops, like mangoes, mustard and vegetables, depend on bees. Explain why declining bee populations are a concern for India, and suggest two actions to help.
questions.modelAnswer: Bees pollinate many crops. Without pollination, flowers don't get fertilised, so fewer fruits and seeds form, reducing harvests, farmers' incomes and food supplies. Actions: reduce the use of harmful pesticides and spray only when bees are not active; plant flowering hedges and trees near fields; support beekeeping, which also gives honey and income.
rubric: Links bees to pollination and crop yield
questions.explain: Criterion D: food security and ecology.

questions.prompt: Seedlings growing right under their parent tree are thin and weak. Why?
options: Competition with the parent for light, water and nutrients

questions.explain: Seeds from flowers come from sexual reproduction.

questions.prompt: Which part of a flower becomes the seed?
questions.explain: And the ovary becomes the fruit.

questions.text: Insects such as bees that carry pollen between flowers are called ___.
questions.explain: Birds and bats can be pollinators too.
